primitives.name: Possession-Level Regularized Adjusted Plus-Minus
primitives.verbatim_quote: org/abs/2605.24056) | NBA | 8/7/6 | 21 | First possession-level RAPM database for 1984-96 (2,179 games reconstructed so far).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'i': 'player index, dimensionless', 'p': 'possession index, dimensionless', '\\Delta W_p': 'change in win probability during possession p, unitless', 'P_i': 'player i is on court during possession p, boolean'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear additive model of player contributions, conditional independence of possessions given player state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When possession-level data is sparse or missing, fallback to game-level aggregation.

layer2.mapping: Maps individual player impact to team-level win probability shifts using kernel regression over time-series of possession outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Expected value of win probability change conditioned on player presence.

primitives.name: Bayesian Mediation of Ability, Performance, and Winning
primitives.verbatim_quote: | Package | Latest | Date | Note | |---|---|---|---| | sportsdataverse (PyPI) | 0.2.0b1 | 2026-10-26 | Only sports package with a release in the past 7 days.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'W': 'winning outcome, boolean', 'A': 'ability parameter, unitless', 'P': 'performance variable, unitless'}
primitives.assumptions: Ability mediates performance which then influences winning outcomes via a Bradley-Terry link.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When observed performance data is noisy or unrepresentative, posterior estimates may diverge.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a causal Bayesian network where ability acts as latent variable mediating performance-to-winning paths.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior distribution over ability given observed performance and win outcomes.

primitives.name: Temporal Event Modeling Kernel

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t_1, t_2': 'time points, seconds', '\\gamma': 'kernel bandwidth, s^{-2}', 'K': 'temporal similarity kernel, unitless'}
primitives.assumptions: Events follow Gaussian temporal correlation structure with decay governed by bandwidth parameter.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Kernel becomes degenerate when inter-event intervals exceed characteristic timescale.

layer2.mapping: Used to define transition probabilities between game states in a continuous-time stochastic process.
layer2.telemetry: Kernel-weighted average of event sequences for predicting next state.

reasoning_traces.think:
The three primitives form a coherent mathematical foundation for modern sports analytics. Possession-level RAPM provides granular attribution of player impact through expected win probability shifts, assuming linear additivity and conditional independence across possessions. Bayesian mediation bridges latent ability to observable performance and outcomes, leveraging a Bradley-Terry model to ensure probabilistic consistency. Temporal event modeling uses a Gaussian kernel to encode dependencies among sequential actions, enabling dynamic state transitions. These operators interact through shared variables like time and player presence, forming a dual system: one grounded in static attribution (RAPM), another in dynamic mediation (Bayes), and third in temporal evolution (kernel). Failure modes arise from data sparsity in RAPM, misalignment in mediation assumptions, and kernel bandwidth selection in temporal modeling. The interplay suggests a unified framework where player-level contributions inform tactical decisions via probabilistic inference.
